newsitem.title: UK: Tesco says like-for-like sales up 7.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tesco says like-for-like sales up 7.5 pct.

text.p: British supermarket group Tesco Plc said like-for-like sales in the first five weeks of its second half from August 10 were up 7.5 percent over a year ago.
It said inflation in its stores was currently 3.5 percent giving underlying volume growth of four percent.
Tesco said total UK sales were up 13 percent in the five-week period, adding that the company had "maintained our outperformance against the industry average."
Tesco said like-for-like sales in the first half were up seven percent on underlying volume growth of three percent. It said market share rose to 14 percent from 13 percent last year.
But a petrol price war in the UK "significantly affected petrol profits and overall UK operating margins."
The company saw first half pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits climb to 321 million stg from 290 million stg previously and paid out an interim dividend of 3.25 pence, up from 3.05 pence.
It said the UK "remains very competitive."
But it added that there were good prospects for the group and it would continue to develop its business.
"We believe this will enable us to maintain our momentum. We look forward to reporting a satisfactory outcome for the full year," the company said in a statement.
Tesco said it expected to open 32 new stores in the full year and make extensions totalling 120,000 square feet, giving total new space of 718,000 square feet.

The company said the number of customers signed up for its ClubCard Plus payment card, introduced in July as a follow-on to its ClubCard loyalty card, was "already ahead of our target for the first full year."
